text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.2% today as oil prices declined for a fifth consecutive day on growing hopes for a U.S.-Iran diplomatic resolution. Reports that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if the U.S. eases military pressure fueled optimism for a peaceful settlement, reversing the geopolitical risk premium that had pushed crude higher. With U.S. oil dropping to $107 per barrel, refiners face lower feedstock costs but also compressed margins on the products they sell.

The uncertainty itself is weighing on the stock. Wall Street's own commodity teams have admitted they don't know which direction oil will move next, making it harder for investors to price in refiner earnings. Meanwhile, the Trump administration is exploring a diesel export ban to address high fuel costs for farmers and truckers—a potential headwind if it limits a major revenue stream for U.S. refiners, even as domestic refineries run at a robust 96.8% capacity.
